parent_formulations.source_text: For a positively graded ring S and homogeneous element f of positive degree, S_(f) denotes the degree-zero subring of the graded localization S_f, consisting of fractions a/f^n with deg(a)=n·deg(f).

reviewed_cases.candidate_context: Graded algebra: degree-zero component of the localized graded ring S_f, closed under ring operations, with homogeneous fractions a/f^n satisfying deg(a)=n deg(f).
reviewed_cases.reason: The source defines S_(f) itself as the degree-zero subring of S_f, while the candidate context repeats the specific homogeneous-fraction construction. Resolving this candidate to the source's own meaning would make its definition refer to itself.
reviewed_cases.allowed_next: A generic degree-zero component of a graded ring can be a separate reusable prerequisite if sourced and modeled without the parent-specific localization; preexisting ordinary localization and graded-ring dependencies remain valid.

parent_formulations.source_text: For a homomorphism φ:R^m→R^n of finite free modules, its rank is the largest integer r for which the induced exterior-power map ∧^rφ is nonzero (and is zero when φ itself is zero).

reviewed_cases.candidate_context: Multilinear algebra: induced R-linear map ∧^rφ:∧^rR^m→∧^rR^n obtained by applying φ to each factor before exterior multiplication.
reviewed_cases.reason: Stacks §10.102 Definition 10.102.5 literally asks for the maximum r≥0 such that Λ^r φ is nonzero; §10.2 explicitly includes the zero ring. Over R=0 every free module is zero, and Λ^0 φ=id_R is the zero map, so that maximum is over the empty set. The following Stacks sentence declares rank zero when φ=0, implying an extra convention or tacit nonzero assumption for this edge case.
reviewed_cases.allowed_next: Ask for a precise source/additional convention or annotate the boundary case in a later sourced variant: e.g. rank zero for zero maps as an explicit override, without silently excluding the zero ring from the entire corpus. Do not change ∧^r functor semantics.

parent_formulations.source_text: For a ring R, K_0(R) is the abelian group generated by finite projective R-modules up to isomorphism, modulo [P⊕Q]=[P]+[Q], equivalently modulo split short exact sequence relations among these modules.

occurrences.phrase: abelian group presentation by direct sums

reviewed_cases.candidate_context: Algebraic K-theory: group completion of the commutative monoid of isomorphism classes of finitely generated projective R-modules under direct sum, imposing [P⊕Q]=[P]+[Q] (equivalently split exact relations).
reviewed_cases.reason: The parent defines K_0(R) using finite projective module classes modulo direct-sum relations; the candidate repeats this exact specialized group completion. Candidate-to-parent resolution introduces a defining self-edge.
reviewed_cases.allowed_next: Model abstract group completion of a commutative monoid separately, with finite-projective classes instantiating that monoid; keep K'_0 constructions and their exact-sequence relations distinct.

parent_formulations.source_text: For a commutative ring R and ideal I, its I-adic completion R^ is the inverse limit of the quotient rings R/I^n over positive integers n, with transition maps given by reduction modulo smaller powers.

occurrences.phrase: inverse limit of the quotient rings

reviewed_cases.candidate_context: Commutative algebra: inverse limit of the projective system of commutative quotient rings R/I^n with compatible quotient maps, consisting of tuples (r_n) satisfying r_{n+1} mod I^n=r_n and componentwise ring operations.
reviewed_cases.reason: The I-adic ring completion is the ring inverse limit of the specific quotient system R/I^n. The missing candidate describes this same limit, so identity resolution to its own I-adic completion parent would yield self-dependence; the parent already has a generic category-limit existing link.
reviewed_cases.allowed_next: If the existing generic category limit target is correctly typed for ring systems, its inherited ring structure and transition maps remain in the parent; an independent inverse-limit-of-rings reusable operation may still be useful but must not be resolved to the specialized completion meaning.

parent_formulations.source_text: Let R⊆S be an inclusion of commutative rings with identity, and let x∈S. The element x is strongly transcendental over R if for every integer n≥0, coefficients a_0,…,a_n∈R, and u∈S, the equation u(a_0+a_1x+⋯+a_nx^n)=0 implies ua_i=0 for every i=0,…,n.

reviewed_cases.candidate_context: Ring theory: zero divisor in a commutative ring S, a nonzero element participating in a product of two nonzero elements that equals 0; source's arbitrary multiplier u allows this context.
reviewed_cases.reason: The exact Stacks 10.123.7 formula quantifies over arbitrary u and polynomial coefficients; it neither states the existence of two nonzero factors with zero product nor contains a named zero-divisor prerequisite. The scan-added 'zero-divisor phenomena' phrase is explanatory rather than mathematically required to parse the definition.
reviewed_cases.allowed_next: Propose a guarded, version-bound replacement of this one missing reference by external with an explicit rationale, only after an individual decision and full predecessor review. Preserve ring and inclusion dependencies; never alias to either the zero-inclusive annihilator concept or the nonzero zero-divisor definition.
